overview: Rwookrrorro is a tree-top capital on Kashyyyk, documented across Films · Clone Wars · KOTOR. Rwookrrorro crowns Kashyyyk's wroshyr canopy as Wookiee capital, target of Trandoshan raids and Imperial enslavement operations.
history:
Rwookrrorro began as a tree-top capital anchor on Kashyyyk, positioned where water, ore, hyperspace lanes, or sacred geography forced travelers to stop. Rwookrrorro grew where Kashyyyk's resources—water, ore, kyber, or trade lanes—forced travelers to stop, creating a tree-top capital that outlasted first founders. Early survey maps from the Old Republic era list Rwookrrorro as a mandatory customs point for sector governors and Jedi exploration teams. Films, Clone Wars, Rebels, Mandalorian, Ahsoka, KOTOR, KOTOR II, TOR, and Sith Empire narratives all treat Rwookrrorro as more than scenery—it is a decision point.

Ancient and pre-Republic layers beneath Rwookrrorro include buried fortresses, Rakatan relics, and Sith ward-stones that still disrupt modern sensors. Pre-Republic and Sith-era layers beneath Rwookrrorro include ward-stones, Rakatan markers, and Massassi masonry that modern engineers still discover during repaving. High Republic pathfinders logged Rwookrrorro as a waypoint during the Great Hyperspace Rush, leaving beacon towers that later wars repurposed as artillery spotters. Local archives recovered from Kashyyyk suggest Rwookrrorro once governed trade policy for entire subsectors before centralization on Coruscant.

In the modern era, Rwookrrorro expanded through prefab districts, orbital elevators, and refugee camps that fused multiple species into a single urban rhythm. Clone Wars, Imperial occupation, and New Republic rebuilding each added districts to Rwookrrorro; Mandalorian and Ahsoka-era storylines treat it as a live operational hub. Mandalorian-era bounties and Ahsoka-era investigations repeatedly lead back to Rwookrrorro because its ports lack the scrutiny of Core World bureaucracy. New Republic planners studied Rwookrrorro as a template for rebuilding settlements after the Imperial collapse, citing both its failures and its innovations.

Rwookrrorro has been invaded, liberated, blockaded, and rebuilt more times than most planetary capitals, making its streets a palimpsest of battle damage. Battle dossiers from KOTOR sieges, TOR planetary incursions, and Galactic Civil War raids mark Rwookrrorro as strategically contested on Kashyyyk. Clone Wars dossiers mark Rwookrrorro as strategically vital; Imperial Era governors exploited that same geography to punish rebellious populations. KOTOR-era records and TOR-era campaign logs show earlier iterations of the same struggle—control of Rwookrrorro meant control of Kashyyyk.
significance:
The economy of Rwookrrorro runs on layered industries: docking fees, black-market mediation, sacred tourism, factory output, or casino finance depending on the era. Rwookrrorro's economy mixes legal trade with shadow finance—dock fees, kolto or tibanna exports, scavenging, or casino revenue depending on era and governor. Trade guilds from the Techno Union to the Mining Guild filed competing claims on Rwookrrorro infrastructure during the late Republic. Post-war reconstruction funds often bypass Rwookrrorro officially while flowing through its shadow banks—an open secret among Bothan analysts.

Cultural life in Rwookrrorro mixes planetary tradition with imported habits from every species that ever missed a connection and stayed. Markets, cantinas, and temples in Rwookrrorro blend Kashyyyk native ritual with offworld imports, producing music and cuisine that signal rebel safe houses to trained eyes. Music, food, and festival calendars in Rwookrrorro are used by rebels to signal safe houses and by Imperials to track dissident networks. Jedi historians note that some of the galaxy's quietest acts of mercy—evacuations, forged transit papers, hidden healers—were organized in Rwookrrorro back alleys.

Rwookrrorro influences galactic history disproportionately because leaders, smugglers, and prophets treat it as neutral ground until it suddenly is not. Treaties, betrayals, and superweapon strikes linked to Rwookrrorro altered fleet movements across the Old Republic through Sequel Era conflicts. Scenes set in Rwookrrorro across the saga often mark turning points: treaties signed, betrayals exposed, or the first shot of a regional war. Settlement planners across the Rim still cite Rwookrrorro when arguing for open ports versus fortified capitals—a debate renewed after every occupation.
